name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure — Always Free resources
summary: Two small AMD VMs plus a 1,500 OCPU-hour/month Arm allowance, 200 GB block storage, 20 GB object storage and two autonomous databases, free for the life of the account — not a trial. Signup does ask for a card for identity verification.

verification.observed: Doc page states Always Free resources are free 'for the life of the account'. Enumerates 'up to two Always Free VM instances using the VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro shape', 'the first 1,500 OCPU hours and 9,000 GB hours per month' on VM.Standard.A1.Flex, 'a total of 200 GB of Block Volume storage', '20 GB' object storage, 'two Always Free Oracle Autonomous AI Databases', and one Flexible Load Balancer at 10 Mbps. Fence: the Arm allowance is 'equivalent to 2 OCPUs and 12 GB of memory' for Always Free tenancies. Checked the docs page, not the marketing page — oracle.com/cloud/free returned HTTP 403 to my fetch.

name: Cloudflare Workers — Free plan
summary: 100,000 Worker requests a day at 10 ms CPU each, plus free daily quotas on KV, D1, Queues and Hyperdrive. No card needed to deploy on the free plan.

verification.observed: Pricing page free-plan tables read '100,000 per day' requests and '10 milliseconds of CPU time per invocation'. Workers KV free row: '100,000 / day' keys read, '1,000 / day' written, '1 GB' stored. D1 free row: '5 million / day' rows read, '100,000 / day' rows written, '5 GB (total)' storage. Queues '10,000 operations/day included'. The page states no end date and does not mention a card requirement either way.

name: Cloudflare Workers AI — 10,000 free Neurons per day
summary: A daily allowance of 10,000 Neurons of model inference (Llama, Whisper, embeddings and friends) at no charge, resetting every midnight UTC.

verification.observed: Page reads 'Our free allocation allows anyone to use a total of 10,000 Neurons per day at no charge.' Pricing table row confirms 'Workers Paid | 10,000 Neurons per day | $0.011 / 1,000 Neurons', and 'All limits reset daily at 00:00 UTC.' Neurons are a normalised unit, so what 10,000 buys depends on the model you pick.

name: Vercel Hobby plan
summary: Free hosting with 100 GB fast data transfer, 1M edge requests and 1M function invocations a month — but the terms restrict it to non-commercial, personal use.

verification.observed: Docs page (last_updated 2026-09-14) opens 'The Hobby plan is free and aimed at developers with personal projects'. Included-usage table: 'Fast Data Transfer — First 100 GB', 'Edge Requests — First 1,000,000', 'Function Invocations — First 1,000,000', 'Active CPU — 4 CPU-hrs', 200 projects, 100 deployments per day. Fence, quoted: 'the Hobby plan restricts users to non-commercial, personal use only.' Also 'As the Hobby plan is a free tier there are no billing cycles.'

name: GitHub Copilot Free
summary: A $0 Copilot tier for individual developers: a capped monthly allowance of code completions and chat requests, no card, no trial clock.

verification.observed: Plans page lists 'Free: $0' and describes it as 'a new free pricing tier with limited functionality for individual developers'. Quotas quoted on the page: 'limited to 2000 completions and 50 chat requests (including Copilot Edits)' per month. Eligibility fence, quoted: 'Users assigned a Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise seat are not eligible for access.'

name: GitHub Actions — free minutes on GitHub Free
summary: 2,000 CI minutes and 500 MB of artifact storage a month on a free personal account — and unmetered on standard runners if the repository is public.

verification.observed: Billing doc's included-quota table gives GitHub Free '500 MB' artifact storage and '2,000' minutes per month. Page also states 'GitHub Actions usage is free for self-hosted runners and for public repositories' and 'The use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free: In public repositories.' The public-repo exemption is the larger of the two offers; the 2,000 minutes apply to private repos.

name: GitHub Codespaces — free monthly core hours
summary: A free personal account gets 120 core-hours and 15 GB-month of Codespaces every month — a real cloud dev box, not a trial.

verification.observed: Billing doc's table 'Free and billed use by personal accounts' lists '120 hrs' compute time and '15 GB-month' storage for GitHub Free. Core-hours, not wall-clock hours: a 2-core machine burns the 120 in 60 hours, a 4-core in 30.

name: Hugging Face Spaces — free CPU and ZeroGPU hardware
summary: Host a demo app on free hardware: 2 vCPU / 16 GB always, and ZeroGPU dynamic GPU time at no cost. Free accounts get no inference credits — those are a PRO thing.

verification.observed: Pricing page Spaces hardware table reads 'CPU Basic: 2 vCPU, 16 GB memory, FREE' and 'ZeroGPU: dynamic resources, Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell up to 96 GB, FREE'. Qualifier: the page lists no free-account inference credits — inference credits appear only under PRO ($9/month, '20× included inference credits'), so do not read this row as free API inference.

name: Supabase Free plan
summary: A free Postgres project with auth and storage: 500 MB database, 1 GB files, 50,000 monthly active users. Projects pause after a week of no traffic, so it suits side projects, not anything that must stay up.

verification.observed: Pricing page Free column reads 'from $0/month', '500 MB database size (Shared CPU • 500 MB RAM)', '5 GB egress', '1 GB file storage', '50,000 monthly active users'. The fence is stated on the same card: 'Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity. Limit of 2 active projects.'

name: Neon Free plan (serverless Postgres)
summary: Serverless Postgres with branching: 0.5 GB storage and 100 compute-hours per project, up to 100 projects. The page states outright that it is permanent and needs no card.

verification.observed: Pricing page Free column: '$0/month', '0.5 GB/project' storage, '100 CU-hours/project', '100' projects, '10' branches per project. Quoted directly from the page: 'The Free plan is permanent (not a trial); no credit card required.'

name: OpenRouter — :free model variants
summary: Any model ID ending in :free costs nothing per token, but you get 50 requests a day until you have bought $10 of credit at some point, after which it is 1,000 a day. 20 requests/minute either way.

verification.observed: Limits doc: free variants (IDs ending ':free') are capped at 50 requests per day for accounts with 'Less than 10' credits purchased all time, and 1,000 requests per day at 'At least 10'. A 20 requests-per-minute cap applies to free variants regardless. The page notes 'The limit tier is selected by all-time credits purchased, independently of is_free_tier.' Fence worth knowing: the 1,000/day tier is only reachable after a one-time $10 purchase, so the genuinely-free ceiling is 50/day.

name: Cohere trial API keys
summary: A free API key for Cohere's chat, embed and rerank endpoints, capped at 1,000 calls a month. Enough to prototype against, not enough to run anything on.

verification.observed: Rate-limits doc states trial keys are 'free but limited in usage' and that 'Trial keys (and prod keys on newer Chat model variants) are limited to 1,000 API calls a month.' Per-endpoint trial rate limits listed range from '5 req / min' to '500 req / min', with Chat models at '20 req / min'. The page did not state a commercial-use restriction, so I am not claiming one.

name: Upstash Redis — Free plan
summary: A serverless Redis database at $0: 500K commands a month, 256 MB of data, 10 GB bandwidth. No card until you deliberately upgrade.

verification.observed: Pricing page Free column: '$0', '500K' commands per month, '256 MB' max data size, '10 GB' bandwidth. Card behaviour is stated as a consequence, not a gate: 'Once you enter your credit card, your database will be upgraded to the pay-as-you-go plan.'

name: Netlify Free plan
summary: Free static and functions hosting on a monthly credit allowance (300 credits), with custom domains, SSL, deploy previews and serverless functions included.

verification.observed: Pricing page Free card reads '$0 forever' with a '300 credit limit', plus 'Unlimited deploy previews', 'Add Custom domains with SSL', 'Functions & AI models', 'Global CDN'. Note the shape change: Netlify now meters the free plan in credits rather than the old bandwidth/build-minute numbers, and this page does not state what 300 credits buys in GB or minutes.

name: MongoDB Atlas — M0 free cluster
summary: A free-forever shared MongoDB cluster with 512 MB of storage, capped at roughly 100 operations per second.

verification.observed: Pricing page M0 card reads 'Free forever', '$0/hour', '512MB of storage', 'Shared RAM', 'Shared vCPU'. The page's own FAQ adds: 'Atlas's free tier includes 512 MB of storage, 32MB of sort memory, and up to 100 operations per second.' The page does not say whether a card is required at signup, so I am not claiming either way.

name: Cloudflare R2 — free tier
summary: 10 GB of object storage a month with a million writes and ten million reads, and no egress charge at all — the reason people move buckets off S3.

verification.observed: Pricing page free-tier table: '10 GB-month / month' storage, Class A '1 million requests / month', Class B '10 million requests / month', egress 'Free'. Stated fence: 'The free tier only applies to Standard storage, and does not apply to Infrequent Access storage.'

name: Google Cloud — Free tier plus $300 trial credit
summary: An always-free monthly slice of Compute Engine, Cloud Storage and Cloud Run that never runs out, plus a one-off $300 credit for new accounts to spend over 90 days.

verification.observed: Docs page: 'The Free Trial gets you a $300 Welcome credit to spend over 90 days on various Google Cloud products and you won't be billed.' Free tier rows quoted: Compute Engine '1 non-preemptible e2-micro VM instance per month' in a US region with '30 GB-months standard persistent disk'; Cloud Storage '5 GB-months of regional storage (US regions only) per month'; Cloud Run '2 million requests per month' plus '360,000 GB-seconds of memory, 180,000 vCPU-seconds of compute time'. On overage the page says 'You'll only be billed for usage that exceeds your remaining credit' — billing starts when you upgrade, not automatically at day 90. Recorded as a standing tier: the 90 days is a per-account clock, not an offer end date.

name: AWS Free Tier — $100 signup credit plus always-free services
summary: $100 of credit the moment you open a Free Tier account and up to $100 more for completing activities, on a six-month clock — plus 30+ services that stay free within monthly limits regardless.

verification.observed: Page reads 'When you create a new AWS Free Tier account, you get $100 in credits immediately. As you explore key services, you can earn up to $100 more. That's up to $200 over 6 months.' The fence, quoted: the free plan lasts '6 months after you open it or when your credits run out, whichever comes first.' Separately: '30+ AWS services are always free within monthly usage limits on both the Free and Paid plans.' Standing tier, not a promotion — the six months is per-account, and the page states no offer end date.

name: Microsoft Azure for Students — $100 credit, no card
summary: $100 of Azure credit for full-time university students with no credit card at all, renewable each year you are still a student.

verification.observed: Page states '$100 credit to use on Azure services within 12 months' and 'No credit card required'. Eligibility fence quoted from the page: 'Available only to full-time university students'. Also 'Free monthly amounts of 20+ popular services for 12 months (new Azure customers only)' and 'Free monthly amounts of 65+ always-free services', with 'Renew your subscription annually and continue to get free access to Azure as long as you're a student.'

name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
summary: One student verification unlocks a bundle of otherwise-paid tools at no cost — GitHub Pro, Copilot, $100 of Azure credit, a JetBrains subscription and more.

verification.observed: Pack page lists partner offers including 'Free GitHub Pro while you are a student', 'GitHub Copilot Student is available to verified students', Microsoft Azure '$100 in Azure credit' (18+), JetBrains 'A free subscription for students, to be renewed annually', and Heroku '$13 USD per month credit for 24 months'. No end date is stated; benefits are framed as lasting 'while you are a student'. The page refers to 'verified students' throughout but does not spell out the verification criteria on this page.

name: Gemini API — free tier on Flash models
summary: Gemini Flash and Flash-Lite models are billed at zero on the free tier — real API access, no card. The price is that your free-tier content is used to improve Google's products.

verification.observed: Pricing page headline: 'Start building free of charge with generous limits, then scale up with prepaid then pay-as-you-go pricing.' The Free Tier cells for the Flash models (3.8, 3.7, 3.6, 3.5 Flash and Flash-Lite) read 'Free of charge' for both input and output. The fence is on the same page: free-tier content is 'used to improve our products', which flips to 'Content not used to improve our products' on the paid tier. Per-model rate-limit numbers are not on this page — it points you at AI Studio for your active limits.

name: Deepgram — $200 signup credit
summary: $200 of speech-to-text and text-to-speech credit on a new account with no card asked for, then pay-as-you-go.

verification.observed: Pricing page reads 'Free $200 Credit' alongside 'No credit card required', then 'pay-as-you-go'. The page states no expiry on the credit, so treat depletion rather than a date as the end of it. Recorded as a standing tier for that reason — there is no offer end date on the page to expire against.

name: ElevenLabs Free plan
summary: 10,000 credits a month of text-to-speech, speech-to-text, sound effects and voice design at $0 — but no commercial licence, so it is for prototypes and personal use.

verification.observed: Pricing page Free column reads '$0 per month' with '10k credits per month', listing 'Text to Speech, Speech to Text, Sound Effects, Voice Design, Music, Productions, Image' and '3 Projects in Studio'. The fence: in the plan comparison table 'Commercial use' appears from the Starter tier upward and is absent from the Free row. No attribution requirement was stated on the page I read.

name: Modal Starter — $30/month of free compute
summary: $30 of serverless GPU and CPU compute every month on the Starter plan, renewed monthly rather than a one-off trial pot.

verification.observed: Pricing page Starter plan states '$30 / month free compute'. The page does not say whether a card is required to open a Starter account, so I am not claiming it is card-free. What $30 buys depends entirely on the GPU class you pick — the per-second rates are in the same table.

name: Resend Free plan
summary: 3,000 transactional emails a month at $0 across 3 domains — enough for a side project's signup and password-reset mail.

verification.observed: Pricing page Free column: '$0/mo' with '3,000' emails per month and '3 domains'. The limit that actually bites is stated separately: 'The Free plan is limited to 100 emails per day.' 3,000 a month therefore cannot be spent in a burst.

name: Google Colab — free notebooks
summary: Free hosted Jupyter notebooks with occasional GPU access. Nothing is guaranteed: runtimes cap at 12 hours, idle VMs are deleted, and GPU availability fluctuates.

verification.observed: FAQ answers 'Yes. Colab is free of charge to use.' The qualifiers are on the same page and matter more than the headline: 'Colab resources are not guaranteed and not unlimited, and usage limits sometimes fluctuate', 'access to expensive resources like GPUs is heavily restricted', notebooks 'can run for at most 12 hours, depending on availability and your usage patterns', and 'Virtual machines are deleted when idle for a while, and have a maximum lifetime enforced by the Colab service.'

name: Sentry Developer plan
summary: Free error tracking for one developer: 5,000 errors, 50 session replays and 5M tracing spans a month, with 30 days of history.

verification.observed: Pricing page Developer column: '$0', '5k errors', '50 replays', '5M spans', '30-day lookback'. Described on the page as 'For solo devs working on small projects' and 'Limited to one user' — the single-seat cap is the fence, not the event quota.

name: Mistral Vibe — Free plan with $10/month API credits
summary: Mistral's free Vibe plan comes with a monthly $10 of API credits alongside limited chat and web search — the credits are the useful part.

verification.observed: Pricing page Vibe Free plan lists 'Limited messages and web searches' and '$10 /mo in API credits'. Qualifier: this page covers Vibe, not La Plateforme — it states no free tier for the API itself and links API pricing out to /pricing/api, which I did not open. Read this row as the Vibe plan's credit grant, not as a standing free API tier.

name: Google AI Pro — 12 months free for US college students
summary: A free year of Google AI Pro (worth $19.99/mo) for verified US college students — but a payment method is required at signup and it auto-charges $19.99/month when the year ends unless you cancel.

verification.observed: Google's own announcement states US students get 'one year of Google AI Pro for free', valued at '$19.99/mo', with a redemption deadline of 'December 31, 2026'. Two fences quoted from the same page: 'Valid form of payment required at sign-up' and, after the free year, 'Google AI Pro will automatically charge $19.99/month.' The expiresAt here is the claim deadline stated on the page, not the end of a redeemed subscription.

name: Google AI Plus — 12 months free for students outside the US
summary: A free year of Google AI Plus for verified students in 140+ markets outside the US, with higher Gemini limits and cloud storage. A payment method is required and it auto-charges $4.99/month afterwards.

verification.observed: Claim page served me its Bulgarian locale and reads 'Възползвайте се до 31 декември 2026 г.' — claim by 31 December 2026 — for a '1-годишен план Google AI Plus за учащи без парично заплащане' (one-year Google AI Plus student plan at no charge), listing 2x higher usage limits, 400 GB cloud storage and Gemini Omni access, for 'учащи в колеж на възраст над 18 години' (college students over 18), with eligibility reconfirmed annually. Google's announcement post gives the market fence: 'over 140 markets where Google AI Plus is available, except for in the U.S., Bolivia, Albania, Canada, Macau, Hong Kong, and Tunisia', 'Valid form of payment required at sign-up', and auto-charge of '$4.99/month or local currency equivalent' afterwards. What you see on the page depends on your locale.

name: Groq API — Free plan rate limits
summary: Groq does run a free API plan, but I could not read its actual limits, so do not plan around a number until you have seen your own.

verification.observed: Could not confirm the offer. The rate-limits doc renders a tabbed table with a 'Free Plan Limits' tab, and the surrounding prose ('Upgrade to Developer plan to access higher limits') implies a free plan exists — but the tab's contents did not come through in my fetch, so I have no per-model RPM/RPD/TPM numbers. groq.com/pricing states nothing about a free tier at all. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than guessing at limits I did not see.

name: Akamai Cloud (Linode) — $100 trial credit
summary: $100 of cloud credit for customers who have never taken the free trial before. It has to be spent within the trial period, and GPU plans are excluded.

verification.observed: Landing page offers a 'US$100 credit', 'available only to new customers who have not yet signed up for a free trial'. The FAQ says 'You must spend your service credits during the trial period' but the page does not define how long that period is, and it does not state an offer end date — so this is filed as a standing tier and the duration is left unclaimed rather than guessed. The page also excludes GPU plans from the promotion, and points at a separate 'Promotion Redemption Rules & Conditions' document I did not open.

name: Claude — Free plan
summary: Free Claude on web, desktop and mobile with web search, file creation, code execution and memory across conversations. The page does not publish the usage cap, so expect to hit one without warning.

verification.observed: Pricing page Free column reads 'Free for everyone' and lists 'Chat on web, desktop, and mobile', 'Search the web, create files, and run code', 'Memory across conversations', 'Connect your apps and tools', 'Create Artifacts'. The only thing said about limits is the qualitative 'Free covers everyday questions' — no numeric cap is published on the page, so this row does not claim one. Note this is the Claude app, not API credits.

name: Vercel AI Gateway — free credit tier
summary: Every Vercel team gets monthly free AI Gateway credits usable on a subset of models, at provider list price with no markup. Buying any credit permanently ends the free monthly allowance.

verification.observed: Docs page (last_updated 2026-09-08) states 'Every Vercel team account gets access to both a free tier and a paid tier for AI Gateway Credits' and 'The free tier includes a subset of models, not the full catalog', with free-tier requests 'rate limited per model, with lower limits than the paid tier' returning 429 on overage. The sharp edge, quoted: 'Once you purchase credits, your account transitions to the paid tier and the monthly free credit no longer applies.' Also 'Your free credits start when you make your first AI Gateway request.' The page never states the dollar value of the monthly free credit, so this row does not put a number on it.
